annotation.title_clean: THE NEW COUNCIL OF EUROPE FRAMEWORK CONVENTION AND THE FUTURE OF INTELLIGENT ROBOTS IN ADMINISTRATIVE LAW
annotation.title_en: The New Council of Europe Framework Convention and the Future of Intelligent Robots in Administrative Law
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Handrlica, J.; Šopková, K.; Vonásková, L.
named_instruments_referenced: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Journal article analysing how the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (2024) bears on AI-based administrative decision-making. It argues recent national laws (Germany, Estonia, Czech proposals) are not technology-neutral, whereas the Convention's principle-based design is durable. "Intelligent robots" refers to software decision systems, not physical robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: The Framework Convention is the first binding international AI treaty, covering public authority AI lifecycle activities.
National security and pre-deployment R&D are largely excluded from its scope.
National ADM laws in Germany, Estonia and Czechia are tied to present technology, not technology-neutral.
The Convention's general, principle-based provisions give states discretion and make it future-proof.
It differs from the EU AI Act in issuer, binding force and prescriptiveness.
